title: Wren and the Veil
premise: Quentin Eriksen survives in the Veil, a fog-shrouded valley where magic cannot enter, by stealing memories from travelers and selling them to the memory-brokers who rule the valley's gray market. When a date with a mysterious stranger, Wren, reveals that Quentin appears in a century-old book of prophecies as the one who will either extinguish or rekindle the last dragon-fire, they learn the Veil itself is a cage built by the valley's founders to hide the dragon's dying heart from a war-hungry world. Pursued by the Brokers, who want Quentin's prophesied blood to seal the Veil forever, Quentin and Wren flee through the valley's forgotten depths, uncovering that Quentin's stolen memories include fragments of the dragon's own. In the climax, Quentin chooses to return the dragon's memories and feed the last flame with their own past, burning away the Veil and ending the Brokers' reign, though it costs them every memory of Wren. The novel ends with Wren staying beside a memoryless Quentin, beginning again: 'Tell me your name.'
about_author: Juniper Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten letters in a mountain town that no longer appears on maps. They write fantasy about people who survive by staying small, and the cost of finally standing up.

chapters.title: The Gray Market
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin lifts a soldier's war memories in the fog-bound Veil valley and trades them for bread and rent, establishing the memory-broker economy and the rule that magic cannot follow inside. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness; Quentin has sold so many memories they no longer remember their mother's face.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Lamplight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Wren arrives in the valley asking odd questions about dragon-fire, and Quentin, intrigued, agrees to a date partly to pick their memories. The beat is flirtation laced with professional suspicion; for once Quentin wants to keep a memory instead of selling it.

chapters.title: What the Book Remembered
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the Brokers' archive, where Quentin fences stolen memories, they find a prophecy book from a century ago bearing their own face and name beside the last dragon. The beat is vertigo: the invisible life was never invisible.

chapters.title: Wren's True Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals themself as the dragon's last warden, sent to find the prophesied one before the Brokers do, and admits the date was a mission. The beat is betrayal curdling into reluctant alliance as Brokers' hunters close in on Quentin's lodgings.

chapters.title: The Brokers' Kindness
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Broker-Head Maren Voss offers Quentin protection and comfort in exchange for a drop of their prophesied blood, framing it as civic duty. The beat is seductive safety; Quentin, who has never been offered belonging, nearly says yes.

chapters.title: Running the Underfog
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Quentin and Wren flee into the Underfog, the drowned tunnels beneath the valley, pursued by Voss's memory-hounds that track stolen thoughts. The beat is terror and exhilaration; Quentin discovers the stolen memories in their head can confuse the hounds.

chapters.title: The Founder's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a drowned chapel, Wren explains the Veil was built by founders who hid the dragon's dying heart to starve the world's war-magic, and that the Brokers now hoard that power. The beat is moral complexity: the cage was built as mercy and rotted into tyranny.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin realizes fragments among their stolen stock are the dragon's own memories—fire, flight, a name in a dead tongue—planted in the valley's memory-trade generations ago. The beat is uncanny intimacy with a creature Quentin has never met.

chapters.title: The Village of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair reaches a hidden settlement of people the Brokers erased, who recognize the dragon's memories in Quentin and offer shelter. The beat is the first taste of belonging Quentin has ever known, making the coming sacrifice sharper.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer, Repeated
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Voss's hunters capture Wren, and Voss offers Quentin a trade: Wren's life for Quentin's blood and the dragon-memories, promising to reseal the Veil forever. The beat is a trap dressed as mercy, and Quentin sees the cage clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: What Quentin Steals for Love
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin breaks into the Brokers' vault using every trick of their trade, stealing back Wren and the prophecy book itself. The beat is triumph shadowed by dread, because the book's final page shows the prophesied one burning.

chapters.title: The Price on the Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads the prophecy's ending aloud: the one who feeds the fire pays with everything they remember. Wren tries to leave alone to spare Quentin. The beat is quiet heartbreak and Quentin's refusal to be protected from their own choice.

chapters.title: The Heart Beneath the Valley
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Descending to the dragon's heart, a guttering coal beneath the valley's roots, they find Voss already there with an army of memory-hollowed soldiers. The beat is dread as the Brokers move to smother the fire and rule an eternal Veil.

chapters.title: Battle of Borrowed Selves
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin fights the hollowed soldiers by flooding the air with the dragon's stolen memories, waking fragments of selfhood in them. The beat is fierce compassion as a weapon; some soldiers turn on Voss, remembering who they were.

chapters.title: Maren Voss's Own Stolen Years
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Cornered, Voss reveals she was once an erased child of the valley who clawed her way to power by hoarding others' pasts, and she believes only a sealed Veil keeps the world's wars out. The beat is tragic conviction; she is what Quentin could become.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Coal
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With the fire seconds from guttering, Quentin must feed it the dragon's memories and their own, or let Voss smother it and the valley stay safe and small forever. The beat is the novel's moral crux: survival versus a self worth surviving as.

chapters.title: Everything I Remember
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, climax. Quentin pours their memories—mother's face, every theft, Wren—into the last dragon-fire, which roars awake and burns the Veil's fog away as Voss's power crumbles. The beat is transcendent loss; Quentin saves the world and forgets why they wanted to.

chapters.title: Ash and Morning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The valley opens to the sky for the first time in a century; the freed dragon rises, the erased villagers are remembered by the world again, and Voss, hollowed by her own hoarded memories, wanders off unremembered. The beat is exhausted, grieving dawn.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Hillside
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Quentin alive but blank, a stranger in their own skin, sitting where the fog used to be. The beat is aching tenderness; Wren chooses to stay rather than mourn the person Quentin was.

chapters.title: Tell Me Your Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren begins telling Quentin their shared story from the beginning, testing which memories the fire left as embers. The beat is fragile hope: a single fragment of Wren's name surfaces in Quentin's mind, proof something survived.

chapters.title: The First New Memory
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin, relearning the world, makes a first choice that is wholly their own: they refuse a Broker's surviving agent's offer to trade memories again, and instead gives a stolen memory back to its rightful owner. The beat is identity rebuilt through action, not recollection.

chapters.title: Wren and the Veil
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Seasons later, Quentin and Wren live in the open valley among the remembered, where Quentin keeps a shop that returns stolen memories for free. The final beat: Quentin still doesn't remember falling in love, but every morning they choose it again.
